findings.description: ClusterPolicy verify-image-signatures declared twice: Flux copy (flux-kyverno-policies/cosign-policy.yaml, schema-valid) and tofu count-gated copy carrying the `key: cosign.pub` field that the Flux copy documents as rejected by the Kyverno v1.17 CRD. Fresh cluster: count=0, tofu copy never created. Warm cluster: the recovery the comment prescribes (main.tf:234-236, re-run k8s-security-apply) sets count=1 and applies the invalid YAML -> apply fails or clobbers Flux's valid policy. Double owner = the ADR-028 bug class.

metadata.fix: delete stacks/security/verify-images.yaml + data.kubernetes_resources.kyverno_clusterpolicy_crd + resource.kubectl_manifest.cosign_verify_policy (main.tf:228-257); tofu state rm FIRST on any cluster where count=1, else the next apply destroys Flux's policy (same object name)

findings.description: deploy_stack anchor runs a naked `tofu apply` (no -target, no wait, no pki_state_password) — a second encoding of the pipeline order that already diverged from the Makefile in 3 places. pki_state_password is required-without-default (identity/variables.tf:21, storage/variables.tf:19) so deploy-identity and deploy-storage fail on push:main with 'No value for required variable'; the CI deploy path has never gone green on those steps.

metadata.fix: add -var="pki_state_password=$$TF_HTTP_PASSWORD" to the deploy_stack anchor (storage has a real need for it); identity's need disappears with HANOI2-005. After HANOI2-003/004/005 the Makefile recipes collapse to naked applies too — one order, encoded once.

findings.description: identity (198-207) and security (219-227) each run 3 phases (apply -target -> kubectl wait --for=create secret -> full apply) to wait for a CNPG secret that NO tofu resource reads. identity/main.tf has zero data "kubernetes_secret"; the only consumer of identity-pg-app is the PushSecret in flux/external-secrets-kratos.yaml:45, which is Flux-owned and never applied by tofu. The DSN moved to ESO in ADR-028 (main.tf:195-198) — the wait is a fossil of the removed data source. Cost: +2 applies, +2 blocking waits per fresh deploy, and a naked `tofu apply` is illegal outside make.

metadata.fix: one apply per stack, no kubectl wait. Verified invariant: -target=identity_pg_cluster pulled identity_pg_certs in via depends_on (main.tf:167-171), so the 'certs before Cluster CR' ordering (main.tf:86-93) is in the graph, not in the -target — a full apply preserves it.
metadata.security_caveat: security's PushSecret IS tofu-applied; removal relies on ESO retrying on refreshInterval, which the code's own comment (main.tf:220-223) states as the design. Observe on a fresh deploy.

findings.description: k8s-up pre-applies -target=kubernetes_namespace.storage before pki. Fossil of Fix #4: the real origin (git cc66be0) was deploying local-path-provisioner before pki; it lives in the cni stack now, which the Makefile admits at 431-433 while keeping the -target and back-filling a FALSE justification (l.429 'cnpg-s3 secret target ns') — cnpg-s3-credentials is written by storage into the identity namespace (storage/main.tf:256,265), and pki seeds garage/harbor into OpenBao (pki/secrets.tf:211-218), nothing into ns/storage. Side effect: garage-chart is curl+untarred twice per k8s-up (l.428 then l.439).

data.terraform_remote_state.pki + locals.secrets (30-46) have zero references in the stack — the 4 secrets flow through OpenBao/ESO since ADR-028 (comment at main.tf:195-198). The dead state read keeps pki_state_password required, which forces K8S_PKI_REMOTE_STATE_VARS in the Makefile, makes a naked `tofu apply` impossible, and breaks CI's deploy-identity (HANOI2-002).

metadata.fix: delete the data source, locals.secrets, and the 3 pki_state_* variables (~18 lines)

findings.description: The Talos machine-config patch — the lowest disk in the tower, sealed at node creation — redirects 6 registries to rg.fr-par.scw.cloud/st4ck-mirror, a SCR namespace created by stacks/registry-mirror/, which no make target, no STACKS entry and no CI step ever applies. Prerequisite never played: every pull to those 6 registries first tries a mirror the pipeline does not guarantee (Talos falls back to upstream, so pulls succeed — at one wasted round-trip each). Region hardcoded while contexts are region-scoped (all contexts are fr-par today; the first nl-ams arms it). Benefit already measured as marginal: roadmap.md:533-539 corrects the hypothesis (PKI pulls are 30-60s, not 10 min).

metadata.fix: remove registry_mirror_scr_patch from envs/scaleway/main.tf:133 common_config_patches + delete the stack + scripts/mirror-images-to-scr.sh. KEEP patches/registry-mirror.yaml (gcr fallback, no infra dep) and scripts/mirror-images.txt (live input to hauler-manifest-gen.py:32). ADR-034 phase 2 (hauler serve registry) takes over with an endpoint that is in the pipeline.

findings.description: oidc-register still not chained into scaleway-up (l.927) — one forgettable manual gesture per fresh deploy, and K8s OIDC login is silently broken until someone notices.

findings.description: STACKS list is inverted: stacks/external-secrets (zero .tf files — ESO is tofu-owned inside pki since ADR-033) IS listed; stacks/registry-mirror (4 .tf files) is NOT. `make validate` validates an empty directory and skips the only uncovered stack. .woodpecker.yml:14-15 already fixed its own list — a third Makefile/CI divergence.

Pass-1 #2 (Talos bump = 2 coordinated edits) was papered over, not closed: the two pins were ALIGNED on v1.12.9 (contexts/_defaults.yaml:13, envs/scaleway/image/variables.tf:22) but SCW_IMAGE_VARS still does not pass talos_version. Aligning is not deriving — the next bump can silently desync (image built from vX, machine config declaring vY).

metadata.fix: add -var="talos_version=$(shell sed -n 's/^ *talos_version: "\(.*\)"/\1/p' contexts/_defaults.yaml)" to SCW_IMAGE_VARS — same one-liner convention already used for GARAGE_CHART_VERSION at Makefile:238

strengths.note: Macro-order of the pipeline remains correct and legal: cni first, pki before identity, flux-bootstrap last. Bug #31 (PN owned by CI) still fails fast at plan time.
Pass-1 registry findings (#1 vars.mk, #3 garage, #4 cilium, #5 management-eso corpse, #6 VMRule count-gate) are all genuinely closed — verified in-tree, not just claimed.

The two-phase Flux Kustomization split (declared ordering, not retry) is the right primitive and is now used in 4 places. The seed-then-share convention (tofu day-1 + Flux day-2 on the SAME file) is sound — cosign_externalsecrets applies it correctly.
